pr_body:
- `ResettableValueTaskSource` now propagates exceptions immediately from `GetResult`. I.e.: if it gets set successfully without `final` (via e.g. RECEIVE) and then with exception with `final` (via `AbortRead`) it'll report the exception from the abort. cc @CarnaViire 
- Added comments for `QuicStream` and both task sources
- Added some more tests (for `RemoteCertificate`, for `Task` properties of `QuicStream`)

Fixes #72027

review_comments:
I think we've discussed previously that we also needed a transition
```
// Ready -> [TrySetException(final: true)] -> Completed(never leaves this state)
```
That discards whatever was ready inside because the whole thing was aborted.

Do I remember wrongly?

I solved the issue with abort differently since I need to know whether `_valueTaskSource` was set or not (it needs to be reset before setting another result and user already has a `ValueTask` with the current token). So we keep the `Ready` state, but later in `GetResult` we propagate the error - I mean throw immediately if final task is exceptional - from `_finalTaskSource` and do the `Ready` --> `Completed` transition (that's the last line in the comment).
I.e. the transition you're looking for is in `GetResult`.

Also we cannot discard "whatever was in it". If there was an exception, that needs to take precedence. E.g. for cancellation, we would lose `OperationCanceledException` in favor of `QuicException(QuicError.OperationAborted)`

| task | | | | |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| _valueTaskSource | success | fail E1 | success | fail E1 |
| _finalTaskSource | success | success | fail E2 | fail E2 |
| GetResult  | success | fail E1 | fail E2 | fail E1 |
| GetResult subsequent  | success | success | fail E2 | fail E2 |

Why inner exception? 🤔 Above we were just setting  `_finalTaskSource.TrySetException(exception)` to whatever exception was passed to `ResettableValueTaskSource.TrySetException(exception, final: true)`
`_finalTaskSource.Task.Exception` is `AggregateException`, so I'm pulling the original exception from it via `InnerException`.
